title: Quick Start
text:
Starting the Viewer
The AI-Viewer is a static HTML application that runs via any HTTP server. The simplest approach uses Python’s built-in server.

Step 1: Start the Server
# Navigate to project root (parent of ai-viewer and pdai)
cd /path/to/2026project

# Start HTTP server on port 4100
python -m http.server 4100






Important



Important: The server must run from the project root, not from inside ai-viewer or pdai. This ensures both the viewer and document data are accessible.




Step 2: Open Your Browser
Navigate to: http://localhost:4100/ai-viewer/viewer.html
You’ll see the home catalog with all available documents from pdai/index.json.


Step 3: View a Document
Click “View” on any document, or navigate directly:
http://localhost:4100/ai-viewer/viewer.html?doc=pdai/E57
http://localhost:4100/ai-viewer/viewer.html?doc=pdai/Goldbach&page=10

title: Quick Start
text:
Complete Workflow with AI-Scholar
AI-Viewer displays documents processed by AI-Scholar. Here’s the complete workflow:

1. Process the PDF
# OCR processing - creates pages/page_NNN/ structure
ai-scholar process ../pdai/E57/E57.pdf --model gemini-3-flash-preview


2. Run Segmentation
# Identify logical structure - creates manifest.json
ai-scholar segment ../pdai/E57


3. Add Translations (Optional)
# Translate to English - creates pages/page_NNN/page_NNN_translation_english.xml
ai-scholar agent ../pdai/E57 translation-english --pages 0-50


4. View the Result
# Start server from project root
cd /path/to/2026project
python -m http.server 4100

# Open browser
open "http://localhost:4100/ai-viewer/viewer.html?doc=pdai/E57"

title: Installation
text:
Installation
AI-Viewer is a static HTML application that requires only an HTTP server. No Python package installation is strictly necessary.

Method 1: Direct Use (Recommended)
Simply serve the project directory with any HTTP server:
# Navigate to project root
cd /path/to/2026project

# Start Python HTTP server
python -m http.server 4100

# Open browser
open http://localhost:4100/ai-viewer/viewer.html


Method 2: Package Installation
For Python integration and CLI tools:
# Navigate to ai-viewer
cd ai-viewer

# Install in development mode
pip install -e .

# Verify installation
python -c "from ai_viewer import quick_serve; print('OK')"


Method 3: Using uv (Fastest)
# Install uv if not present
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

# Install ai-viewer
cd ai-viewer
uv pip install -e .

Problem
The viewer was displaying content from the next page instead of the current page. When navigating to page 6, it showed content from page 7.

Root Cause
Mismatch between page numbering and file indexing:

Viewer UI: Uses 1-based page numbers (Page 1, Page 2, …, Page 217)
File system: Uses 0-based indices (page_000.png, page_001.png, …, page_216.png)

Before the fix:
// Page 6 in UI
const paddedNum = String(6).padStart(3, '0');  // "006"
const imagePath = `page_006.png`;  // ❌ This is the 7th image (index 6)!
Result: Page 6 loaded page_006.png (7th image) instead of page_005.png (6th image).

Mapping Table
Correct mapping between UI page numbers and file indices:

Testing

Verification Steps

Open Page 1: Should show first page content (title page or introduction)
Open Page 6: Should show 6th page content (not 7th)
Navigate through pages: Each page number should match its content
Check last page: Page 217 should show page_216.png and page_216.html



Test Commands
# Test page 1
open "http://localhost:4100/ai-viewer/application/main_viewer.html?doc=kotschka&page=1"

# Test page 6
open "http://localhost:4100/ai-viewer/application/main_viewer.html?doc=kotschka&page=6"

# Test last page
open "http://localhost:4100/ai-viewer/application/main_viewer.html?doc=kotschka&page=217"

Impact on Other Documents
This fix applies to all documents in the viewer. Any document using the standard PDAI page-centric structure will now load pages correctly.

Related Issues

Issue 1: PIDX Mismatch in XML
If XML files have incorrect pidx attributes (e.g., page_000.xml with pidx="1"), use the fix_pidx tool:
python src/ai_scholar/fix_pidx.py ../pdai/DocumentName/xml


Issue 2: File Naming Convention
All files must follow the standard naming convention: - Images: page_000.png, page_001.png, …, page_216.png - XML: page_000.xml, page_001.xml, …, page_216.xml - HTML: page_000.html, page_001.html, …, page_216.html
See docs/NAMING_STANDARDS.md for complete specification.

Why This Bug Occurred

Natural Assumption: UI page numbers are typically 1-based (human-friendly)
File System Convention: File indices are 0-based (computer-friendly)
Missing Conversion: Code didn’t convert between the two systems
Off-by-One Error: Classic programming mistake when mixing counting systems

Prevention
To prevent similar issues in the future:

Always comment whether variables are 0-based or 1-based
Convert explicitly at boundaries between systems
Test edge cases: Page 1, middle page, last page
Use descriptive names: pageNum (1-based) vs fileIndex (0-based)

Naming Standards: docs/NAMING_STANDARDS.md
PIDX Fix Tool: src/ai_scholar/fix_pidx.py
PDAI Structure: docs/PDAI_STRUCTURE.md

title: PDAI Document Standard
text:
The PDAI (PDF AI) standard defines a structured, portable format for AI-processed PDF documents. PDAI documents are generated by AI Scholar and viewed with AI Viewer.
This specification covers:

Page-centric directory structure
File naming conventions
Manifest format (from segmentation)
Two-level processing (pages and segments)

title: PDAI Document Standard
text:
PDAI Document Structure
All PDAI documents follow a page-centric structure where all files for a page live together:
pdai/DocumentName/
├── DocumentName.pdf              # Original PDF
├── manifest.json                 # Document metadata + segment mappings
├── ai-orchestrator.yml           # Agent configuration
├── css/                          # Display styles
│   └── default.css
├── templates/                    # Document-specific Jinja2 templates
│   └── translation.j2
├── pages/                        # ALL page-level content
│   ├── page_000/                 # Folder per page
│   │   ├── page_000.png          # Page image
│   │   ├── page_000.xml          # OCR XML
│   │   ├── page_000.html         # HTML conversion
│   │   ├── page_000_translation_english.xml   # Agent output
│   │   ├── page_000_translation_german.xml    # Agent output
│   │   └── page_000_fig_1.png    # Extracted figure (if any)
│   ├── page_001/
│   │   ├── page_001.png
│   │   ├── page_001.xml
│   │   └── page_001.html
│   └── ...
└── segments/                     # Document segments (optional)
    └── letters/                  # Segment type folder
        ├── letter_000/           # Folder per segment instance
        │   ├── letter_000.xml
        │   ├── letter_000.html
        │   └── letter_000_translation_english.xml
        └── letter_001/
            └── ...

Design Principles

Page-centric: All derivatives of a page (image, xml, html, translations, figures) share the same stem and live together in pages/page_NNN/
Consistent naming: page_NNN[_agent].ext pattern with underscores only (no hyphens in filenames)
Three-digit padding: page_000, page_001, …, page_999
Segments mirror pages: Same subfolder pattern for logical document segments

title: PDAI Document Standard
text:
File Naming Conventions

Page Files
pages/page_{num:03d}/page_{num:03d}.{ext}
pages/page_{num:03d}/page_{num:03d}_{agent}.xml
pages/page_{num:03d}/page_{num:03d}_fig_{n}.png
Examples:

pages/page_000/page_000.png - First page image
pages/page_042/page_042.xml - Page 42 OCR result
pages/page_005/page_005_translation_english.xml - English translation of page 5
pages/page_012/page_012_fig_1.png - First figure on page 12



Segment Files
segments/{type}/{type}_{num:03d}/{type}_{num:03d}.xml
segments/{type}/{type}_{num:03d}/{type}_{num:03d}_{agent}.xml
Examples:

segments/letters/letter_000/letter_000.xml - First letter
segments/letters/letter_000/letter_000_translation_english.xml - Translation
segments/chapters/chapter_003/chapter_003.xml - Third chapter

title: PDAI Document Standard
text:
Two Processing Levels
PDAI supports processing at two levels:

1. Page-Level (Default)
Agents operate on individual pages:
pages/page_000/page_000.xml → pages/page_000/page_000_translation_english.xml


2. Segment-Level
After segmentation, agents can operate on logical segments:
segments/letters/letter_000/letter_000.xml → segments/letters/letter_000/letter_000_summary.xml

Python API

PdaiPublicationServer
Main server class for serving PDAI documents.

Constructor
from ai_viewer import PdaiPublicationServer

server = PdaiPublicationServer(
    document_path="../pdai/E57",
    host="127.0.0.1",
    port=5100,
    debug=False
)
Parameters:



Parameter
Type
Default
Description




document_path
str
required
Path to PDAI document directory


host
str
“127.0.0.1”
Server host address


port
int
5100
Server port number


debug
bool
False
Enable debug mode





Methods

start()
Start the FastAPI server.
server = PdaiPublicationServer("../pdai/E57")
server.start()  # Server runs on http://localhost:5100


stop()
Stop the server gracefully.
server.stop()


get_document_info()
Get information about the loaded document.
info = server.get_document_info()
print(f"Document has {info['page_count']} pages")
Returns: dict with document metadata




PdaiDocument
Class for handling PDAI document format and structure.

Constructor
from ai_viewer import PdaiDocument

doc = PdaiDocument("../pdai/E57")


Methods

load_page(page_number)
Load a specific page from the document.
page_data = doc.load_page(25)
print(f"Page 25 image: {page_data['image_path']}")
Parameters:



Parameter
Type
Description




page_number
int
Page number (0-indexed)



Returns: dict with page data


get_page_count()
Get total number of pages.
count = doc.get_page_count()
print(f"Document has {count} pages")
Returns: int


validate_format()
Validate PDAI format compliance.
validation = doc.validate_format()
if validation['has_images'] and validation['has_html']:
    print("Valid PDAI document")
Returns: dict with validation results


load_manifest()
Load and parse manifest.json.
manifest = doc.load_manifest()
for segment_type in manifest.get('segments', {}):
    print(f"Found segment type: {segment_type}")
Returns: dict with manifest content or None

text:
Integration Examples

Jupyter Notebook
from ai_viewer import quick_serve
from IPython.display import IFrame
import threading

# Start viewer in background
def start_viewer():
    quick_serve("../pdai/E57", port=5100, open_browser=False)

thread = threading.Thread(target=start_viewer)
thread.daemon = True
thread.start()

# Display in notebook
IFrame('http://localhost:5100/doc/E57/viewer', width=1000, height=600)


Flask Integration
from flask import Flask, redirect
from ai_viewer import PdaiPublicationServer
import threading

app = Flask(__name__)

# Start AI Viewer in background
def start_viewer():
    server = PdaiPublicationServer("../pdai/E57", port=5101)
    server.start()

viewer_thread = threading.Thread(target=start_viewer)
viewer_thread.daemon = True
viewer_thread.start()

@app.route('/view/<doc_name>')
def view_document(doc_name):
    return redirect(f'http://localhost:5101/doc/{doc_name}/viewer')


Programmatic Document Access
from ai_viewer import PdaiDocument

# Load document
doc = PdaiDocument("../pdai/E57")

# Get page count
print(f"Pages: {doc.get_page_count()}")

# Load manifest for segment info
manifest = doc.load_manifest()
if manifest:
    segments = manifest.get('segments', {})
    for seg_type, seg_data in segments.items():
        items = seg_data.get('items', [])
        print(f"{seg_type}: {len(items)} items")

# Validate format
validation = doc.validate_format()
print(f"Valid: {validation['valid']}")

title: Viewer Features
text:
Core Features

Universal PDAI Support
AI-Viewer displays any PDAI-compliant document using page-centric structure:
pdai/DocumentName/
└── pages/
    └── page_NNN/
        ├── page_NNN.png
        ├── page_NNN.xml
        ├── page_NNN.html
        └── page_NNN_translation_english.xml

Page-centric loading — All page files from one folder
Consistent naming — page_NNN[_agent].ext pattern
Underscore convention — No hyphens in filenames



High-Quality Display

High-resolution images — Supports 600+ DPI page images
Crisp text rendering — Proper font handling
Zoom capabilities — From 25% to 500%
Smooth scaling — Anti-aliased image display

Development Setup

Prerequisites

Python 3.10 or higher
Git
A PDAI document for testing (e.g., from ai-scholar processing)

# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/grasshoff/ai-viewer.git
cd ai-viewer

# Create virtual environment (optional but recommended)
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate

# Install in development mode
pip install -e .

# Verify installation
ai-viewer --help


Using uv (Recommended)
# Install uv if not present
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

# Install dependencies
cd ai-viewer

text:
Code Standards

Python Style
We follow PEP 8 with these preferences:

Line length: 100 characters maximum
Imports: Standard library, third-party, then local (separated by blank lines)
Docstrings: Google style for functions and classes
No type hints: Keep code clean and simple (per project preference)



Example Code Style
"""Module docstring explaining purpose."""

import os
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import FastAPI

from ai_viewer.exceptions import DocumentNotFoundError


def load_document(path):
    """Load a PDAI document from the specified path.
    
    Args:
        path: Path to the PDAI document directory.
        
    Returns:
        Document object with loaded content.
        
    Raises:
        DocumentNotFoundError: If the path doesn't exist.
    """
    doc_path = Path(path)
    if not doc_path.exists():
        raise DocumentNotFoundError(f"Document not found: {path}")
    
    return Document(doc_path)


JavaScript Style
For viewer JavaScript:

No frameworks: Plain JavaScript only
Readable code: Clear variable names, comments for complex logic
DOM manipulation: Direct DOM access preferred over jQuery-style



HTML/CSS Style

Semantic HTML: Use appropriate elements (<nav>, <main>, <article>)
CSS variables: Use for theming and consistency
Responsive design: Mobile-first approach

title: Footnote Parsing Specification and Assessment Register
text:
Problem: Multi-digit footnote numbers are being split during OCR - Example: 23 becomes 2 3 - Example: 10 becomes 1 0
Solution Required: - Post-OCR processing to detect and merge split numbers - Pattern recognition for sequential digits that should be combined - Context analysis to determine when digits belong together



Requirements: 1. Ordering: Footnotes in the footnote block must be sorted by their numerical sequence 2. Correspondence Check: Every footnote marker in the text body MUST have a corresponding entry in the footnote block 3. Orphan Detection: Footnotes in the block without references in the text should be flagged



Problem: Pages with extensive footnotes (like page 4) show footnotes in the block with no corresponding markers in the text body
Required Checks: - Count footnote markers in text: <fn>1</fn>, <fn>2</fn>, etc. - Count footnotes in block: <footnote data-fn="1">, etc. - Report mismatches and missing references






Purpose: Marks footnote references within the main text body
Syntax: <fn>NUMBER</fn>
Requirements: 1. Number Format: Must contain only digits (1, 2, 3, … 99, etc.) 2. Sequential: Should generally appear in ascending order 3. Unique per Page: Each number should appear only once per page 4. Validation: Must have corresponding <footnote> in footnote block
Parsing Rules:
# Detection pattern for split numbers
# Before: <fn>2</fn> <fn>3</fn> (when meant to be 23)
# After: <fn>23</fn>

# Algorithm:
1. Extract all <fn> tags and their positions
2. Check if consecutive <fn> tags are within X characters
3. If single digits and close proximity, merge them
4. Validate against footnote block for confirmation



Purpose: Contains the footnote text in the footnote block
Syntax: <footnote data-fn="NUMBER">TEXT</footnote>
Requirements: 1. data-fn Attribute: Must match a <fn> marker in the text 2. Sorting: Must be sorted numerically by data-fn value 3. Content: Should not include the footnote number in the text (number is in attribute) 4. Completeness: Every footnote must have non-empty content
Validation Rules:
# Sorting check
footnotes = extract_all_footnotes()
sorted_footnotes = sorted(footnotes, key=lambda x: int(x.data_fn))
assert footnotes == sorted_footnotes, "Footnotes not in sequence"

# Correspondence check
text_markers = extract_all_fn_markers()
footnote_numbers = [f.data_fn for f in footnotes]
assert set(text_markers) == set(footnote_numbers), "Mismatch between markers and footnotes"



Purpose: Contains all footnotes for a page
Syntax:
<footnotes>
  <footnote data-fn="1">First footnote text</footnote>
  <footnote data-fn="2">Second footnote text</footnote>
  ...
</footnotes>
Requirements: 1. Position: Must appear at the bottom of the page content 2. Singularity: Only one <footnotes> block per page 3. Completeness: Must contain ALL footnotes referenced in the text 4. Order: Child <footnote> elements must be in numerical order







Page 1: Basic footnotes (1-7) - test simple parsing
Page 4: Complex footnotes with potential split numbers - test merge algorithm
Page with 20+ footnotes: Test sorting and sequence validation
Page with missing references: Test orphan detection




For each page, verify:

Number Integrity: No split multi-digit numbers
Sequence Order: Footnotes sorted 1, 2, 3, …, not 1, 10, 2, 20, 3
Correspondence: Every <fn>X</fn> has matching <footnote data-fn="X">
No Orphans: No footnotes without text references
No Duplicates: Each footnote number appears exactly once
Content Validity: All footnotes have non-empty content
XML Validity: Well-formed XML structure

  "page": 4,
  "errors": [
    {
      "type": "split_number",
      "location": "text",
      "found": ["<fn>2</fn>", "<fn>3</fn>"],

    },
    {
      "type": "missing_reference",
      "footnote_number": "15",
      "in_block": true,
      "in_text": false
    },
    {
      "type": "sequence_error",
      "found_order": [1, 10, 11, 2, 3],
      "correct_order": [1, 2, 3, 10, 11]
    }
  ]
}

CRITICAL: Implement correspondence validation
HIGH: Add sequence sorting to footnote blocks
HIGH: Create validation report for each page
MEDIUM: Add visual indicators for validation errors
MEDIUM: Implement auto-correction where possible

Run validation suite
Generate error report
Compare accuracy rates
Document model-specific issues

Red: Orphaned footnote (no text reference)
Yellow: Suspected split number

Overview
The viewer now uses external CSS files for document content styling, separating concerns between: - Inline CSS: Viewer UI (navigation, panels, controls) - External CSS: Document content formatting (paragraphs, footnotes, typography)

File Structure

├── application/

├── config/

CSS Organization

1. Inline CSS (main_viewer.html)
Purpose: Viewer UI components and layout
Includes: - Navigation bar styling - Panel layout (dual-pane) - Control buttons - Loading/error states - Glass-morphism effects - Document selection page
Why inline? - Critical rendering path optimization - Viewer UI is tightly coupled to HTML structure - Reduces HTTP requests for initial load


2. External CSS (config/styles/document-content.css)
Purpose: Document content formatting
Includes: - Paragraph spacing and typography - Footnote styling (inline refs + bottom section) - Section headers - Paragraph numbers (<parno>) - Mathematical content - Heading hierarchy
Why external? - Customizable: Users can edit without touching HTML - Reusable: Same styles across different viewers - Version control: Style changes tracked separately - Extension-ready: Easy to package for VSCode/Cursor

<!-- In main_viewer.html -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="../config/styles/document-content.css">

Package Responsibilities

ai-scholar: The Processing Engine
AI-Scholar transforms raw documents into structured, annotated content:
# Core processing commands
ai-scholar process document.pdf         # PDF → pages/page_NNN/
ai-scholar segment ../pdai/DocName      # → manifest.json
ai-scholar agent ../pdai/DocName translation-english  # → pages/page_NNN/page_NNN_translation_english.xml
Generates:

pages/page_NNN/page_NNN.png — High-resolution page images
pages/page_NNN/page_NNN.xml — Structured OCR output (DTD-validated)
pages/page_NNN/page_NNN.html — Viewer-compatible HTML
pages/page_NNN/page_NNN_fig_M.png — Extracted figures
pages/page_NNN/page_NNN_{agent}.xml — Agent processing outputs
manifest.json — Document structure and segment mappings



pdai: The Data Layer
PDAI provides a standardised, page-centric directory structure:
pdai/DocumentName/
├── DocumentName.pdf              # Original source
├── manifest.json                 # Structure metadata
├── ai-orchestrator.yml           # Agent configuration
├── css/                          # Display styles
├── templates/                    # Document-specific templates
├── pages/                        # ALL page-level content
│   ├── page_000/
│   │   ├── page_000.png
│   │   ├── page_000.xml
│   │   ├── page_000.html
│   │   ├── page_000_translation_english.xml
│   │   └── page_000_fig_1.png
│   └── page_001/
│       └── ...
└── segments/                     # Materialised segments
    └── letters/
        ├── letter_000/
        └── letter_001/
Key principle: All files for a page live together in pages/page_NNN/. No scattered directories.


ai-viewer: The Presentation Layer
AI-Viewer serves PDAI documents through an interactive web interface:
# Start server from project root
cd /path/to/2026project
python -m http.server 4100

# Open viewer
open "http://localhost:4100/ai-viewer/viewer.html?doc=pdai/DocumentName"
Provides:

Interactive page navigation (Document mode)
Agent output viewing (Agent mode)
Segment-based browsing (letters, chapters, paragraphs)
MathJax rendering for mathematics
Translation layer selection

Best Practices

Document Preparation

Process documents — Use ai-scholar process for new documents
Migrate old documents — Use ai-scholar migrate for legacy documents
Segment early — Generate manifest.json for navigation
Validate structure — Use ai-scholar assess to check integrity



Viewing Workflow

Start simple — View original HTML first
Check segments — Verify navigation works correctly
Add layers — Run translation/annotation agents as needed
Compare outputs — Switch layers to compare processing results

text:
Troubleshooting

Document Not Loading
# Check structure
ls -la ../pdai/DocumentName/pages/page_000/

# Verify required files
ls ../pdai/DocumentName/pages/page_000/page_000.png
ls ../pdai/DocumentName/pages/page_000/page_000.html


Missing Segments
# Run segmentation
ai-scholar segment ../pdai/DocumentName

# Check manifest
cat ../pdai/DocumentName/manifest.json | jq '.segments'


Agent Outputs Not Showing
# Check page folder
ls ../pdai/DocumentName/pages/page_000/

# Run agent if missing
ai-scholar agent ../pdai/DocumentName translation-english


Server 404 Errors
# Ensure server runs from project root
cd /path/to/2026project  # Parent of ai-viewer and pdai
python -m http.server 4100

title: Three-Package Integration
text:
Summary
The three-package architecture provides clean separation of concerns:

ai-scholar handles all AI processing
pdai stores data in page-centric format
ai-viewer presents content interactively via static HTTP

Data flows from processing through storage to presentation, with all page-related files organised together in pages/page_NNN/ folders.
